title: Building a browser football manager as one HTML file with an AI coding assistant
author: Erdal3666
selftext:
Global Football Manager 2026-2027 is a career football manager that runs in the browser. You pick one club and keep it: tactics board, a live 2D match, transfers, domestic cups, European cups and a World Cup. The same page also has an online mode, where each manager holds one club and the world is shared.

The part that belongs here is how it was built.

Almost all of the code was written with an AI coding assistant, inside one HTML file. That file is now about 60,000 lines. The assistant is good at adding a screen. It is bad at remembering the rules that keep the game from splitting apart. Two of those rules ate most of the time.

The online world has to be the same for every player. Clubs, fixtures and cup draws come from fixed seeds. If a normal random call is left in, two managers in the same season get different worlds and a transfer no longer matches on both sides. Every time a new feature touched world generation, that random lock had to be put back.

The live match and the saved career share one state object. A patch that only changes the match screen can still move wages, the calendar, or a player who was already sold. The workflow that survived is a small patch, then open that exact screen. A full rewrite of the file never survived.

I am not going to dress this up as a clever art pipeline. The useful AI work was the code, and the useful discipline was refusing patches that touched systems I did not ask to change.

It is free in the browser: https://gfm2026-2027.com/

The older itch.io copy stays up as a trial until 30 October 2026.

If you have kept a large single-file game coherent with an assistant, I want to hear what you lock down before you let it edit.
